topic: Strict freshness with one-front auto-merge and atomic landing lease
context: ADR-094 final decision. User-owned repository without native merge queue. Trunk removed. Parallel refresh of 41 branches triggered 820 workflow runs and 818 cancellations. Fixed Git ref acquisition was live-probed: first create succeeded, second returned 422, release removed the ref.

votes.rationale: Strict is the safety lock; the atomic Git-ref lease and one-front rule control concurrency and CI cost.
The lease closes the check-then-arm race and the final protocol covers 422 recovery, stale branches, and post-merge health.
The measured cost model, stacked PR boundary, and fail-closed lease are scoped correctly.
Git ref creation is atomic, concurrent acquisition fails 422, crash recovery fails closed, and governance auto-merge is prohibited.
Live strict state, lease probe, and all operational commands are verifiable.
Minimum mechanism: GitHub strict freshness, one fixed lock ref, no queue, bot, or daemon.
